label: Fleet repair
heading: When a fleet already has a body shop
decision: Can the depot approve a backup shop?
sourceLabel: Full fleet account script for body shops
backlink: Compare the fleet response with two other cold calling examples
intro: A body shop is calling a fleet manager to find out who chooses the repair shop when a van needs bodywork.
opener: When one of your vans needs bodywork, do you choose the shop locally, or does head office handle that?
response: When they’re booked up, can you use a second shop?
yesLabel: If they can use a backup
yesWords: Which vans would you send us first?
yesNote: If the shop can handle those vehicles, ask who approves a first estimate. Offer an introduction to the shop manager once you know there’s a fit.
otherLabel: If head office owns the list
otherWords: Who handles repair vendors for your depot?
otherNote: If the approved list is closed, thank them and end the call. Record what they told you about the vendor list.

label: IT staffing
heading: When a hiring manager has an open IT role
short: You spotted an open IT role
decision: Who owns the hire, and which skill is missing?
sourceLabel: Full IT staffing script for hiring managers
backlink: Compare the hiring-manager response with two other cold calling examples
intro: An IT recruiter saw a contract network administrator opening. The first question checks whether the person who answered owns that hire.
opener: I saw the contract network administrator role in [City]. Are you the one hiring for it?
buyerLine: Yes. We still need someone who can handle the cutover.
response: Which part of the cutover would they need to run on their own?
yesWords: Can you bring in an outside recruiter for that role?
yesNote: If they can, use what you just learned in the second ask. “Would ten minutes on Thursday work to go over the cutover and the start date?”
otherWords: Thanks for letting me know. I’ll take that role off my list.
otherNote: If talent acquisition owns an open role, ask who manages contract suppliers and how they prefer to hear from recruiters.

label: Email follow-up
heading: When your first sales email went unanswered
short: Your sales email got no reply
decision: What information did the buyer actually ask for?
sourceLabel: Full cold call script after an unanswered sales email
backlink: Compare the email follow-up response with two other cold calling examples
intro: A courier rep is making the first phone call after an email about late pickups. The shipping lead needs a specific answer for one depot.
opener: I sent you a note about late pickups. We collect parcels after your usual courier leaves. What happens to orders that miss pickup?
buyerLine: Just send me your Friday cutoff.
response: Sure. Which depot should I check with dispatch?
yesWords: I’ll check the latest Friday pickup for that depot and email it to you.
yesNote: Confirm the address, check with dispatch and send the time you verified. Record an email request.
otherLabel: If everything can wait until morning
otherWords: Sounds like your morning pickup covers it. Thanks for taking my call.
otherNote: Close the call there. A meeting belongs on the calendar when the buyer agrees to a date and time.
